title: Sysmon process integrity checks
summary: A Go detector for ProcessGuid mismatches and activity reported after process termination.

caseStudy.problem: Sysmon telemetry can't be trusted if PIDs mutate or events arrive after a process ends, which can hide tampering.
caseStudy.build: A Go detector records the ProcessGuid for each PID on Event ID 1 and flags a later event that reuses the PID with a different ProcessGuid, plus activity reported after an Event ID 5 termination. It keeps both event time and ingestion time to separate delivery lag from a real inconsistency.
caseStudy.validation: A hit is an anomaly to investigate, not proof of kernel tampering. Next step is replayable test data for normal creation, PID reuse, late events, and mismatched identities.

title: SIEM pipeline tuning
summary: A Cribl pipeline tuned to reduce and normalize security events while preserving fields needed for investigations.

caseStudy.problem: Too much security data drives up SIEM cost and slows investigations, but filtering only helps if it keeps the fields detections and analysts rely on.
caseStudy.build: On a consulting engagement, a Cribl pipeline filtered and normalized events before they reached the SIEM. Ingestion dropped 35%.
caseStudy.validation: Confirmed detections kept their required fields and event types, duplicate and low-value data removed, with a rollback plan for parser and routing changes. Client and environment details are confidential.

title: Cloud detection lab
summary: A cloud SOC lab for testing adversary emulation and detections with Caldera, Splunk MLTK, Elastic ML, and Sigma.

caseStudy.problem: Detection ideas need a safe place to generate real adversary activity and measure what the logs and models actually catch.
caseStudy.build: A cloud SOC lab wiring Caldera, Splunk MLTK, Elastic ML, and Sigma: generate activity with Caldera, test detections across the three, and check the context an analyst would need to investigate an alert.
caseStudy.validation: A personal lab, kept separate from consulting engagements. The GitHub repository has the current setup.
